newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's de Klerk will not seek amnesty -- party.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's de Klerk will not seek amnesty -- party.

text.p: The former ruling National Party (NP) said on Monday its leader F.W. de Klerk would not seek amnesty from South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission probing apartheid crimes.
"Mr de Klerk will not apply for amnesty," party spokesman Jan Bosman told Reuters after a NP Federal Council meeting held to discuss the amnesty process ahead of a May 10 deadline.

The commission, appointed to heal the wounds of apartheid, has heard gruelling testimony about torture and abuse by police and former policemen who have confessed to killing a number of anti-apartheid activists.

But De Klerk, who repudiated apartheid in 1990 and four years later surrendered power to President Nelson Mandela, has repeatedly insisted that he has never been a party to any decision to kill apartheid foes.

"It's a lie that I knew. It's a lie that I was part of any conspiracy to do these terrible things... to assassinate people. How many times much I say it's a lie before people hear me?," he told a news conference in March.

In a statement issued on Monday night, de Klerk said he would meet Nobel peace laureate Desmond Tutu, who chairs the Commission, later this week to discuss the Commission's definitions affecting political leaders.

He said the amnesty process appeared to deal only with individuals who had committed crimes, and not his party's willingness to accept overall political responsibility for the policies of the former NP government.

"Within this framework the amnesty process is not the correct channel for the acceptance of political responsibility for policy...Political leaders who in terms of the law did not commit crimes should therefore find another way of doing this," he added.
De Klerk apologised to the truth commission in August last year for the suffering apartheid had wrought during 48 years of NP rule.
